summary: iter90ft — Supplier keyword matching + syndic-wide catalog + noise-word normalization. Extended /app/backend/tests/test_iter90fs_ft_supplier_manual_match.py with 11 new tests (TestNoiseWordNormalization, TestKeywordMatchingSyndicWide, TestSuppliersCatalogSyndicWide, TestPreviewNameSuggestionsArray, TestFindDuplicateSupplierRegression, TestCommitInvoicesNoNameError). 19/19 tests pass. All spec assertions verified: (a) _norm_name strips 'insurance/belgium/assurance/group/services/...' so 'Baloise Insurance Belgium SA' -> 'baloise'. (b) find_supplier_candidates_by_keyword returns both Gerald Baloise Insurance fiches when syndic=Gerald, with the same-copro fiche ranked first (score bonus +0.15). (c) Chinese Wall STRICT: Alpha searching 'Baloise Insurance' NEVER surfaces Gerald's suppliers (all returned rows have syndic_id=ALPHA_SYNDIC_ID). (d) GET /suppliers-catalog now returns whole-syndic scope with same_copro flag; Alpha never sees Baloise Insurance. (e) POST preview-invoices returns both name_suggestion (backward-compat, subset match => 'Baloise') AND name_suggestions[] (array with 'Baloise' entry same_copro=true score>=1.0). (f) commit-invoices with unknown aux + manual_matches now returns HTTP 200, inserted>=1, no NameError('request') — iter79 blocker CONFIRMED FIXED. (g) find_duplicate_supplier still subset-matches 'Baloise Insurance' <-> 'Baloise'.

minor.issue: Route returns 404 (not registered at top-level under /api). The test had to seed fiscal_years directly in Mongo to unblock commit-invoices for ACP Alpha (no FY existed). Not a regression of iter90ft — pre-existing observation.

Invoice documents persisted do NOT retain the input `external_ref` field (only internal_reference is stored). This bit the iter79 test that relied on external_ref for lookup. Not blocking the feature; noted as a data-model observation.

Orphan 440xxx detection still reads s.get('pcmn_account_number') instead of tier_account_number — flagged in iter79 as pending; NOT fixed in this iter (per request). Preview test still asserts orphan detection on OrphanCorp works, but real-supplier false-positives remain.

_norm_name noise-word list now conflates brand identity with legal form — e.g. any two suppliers named 'Group X' & 'Group Y' remain distinct because non-noise word differs, but be aware that adding 'services' as noise may create false duplicates ('AB Services' <-> 'AB Cleaning' still stay distinct — safe). Consider unit-covering a few more edge cases (e.g. 'Corp' as sole token).
